cacheCleared.message: Cache cleared – the mails can be scanned again.

cfUndoHint.message: They go to the trash – you can restore them right after via “Undo”.

clearCacheBody.message: Deletes $1 saved scores and $2 newsletter checks. The mails then show as unscored and can be scanned again – with paid models this costs again.

costUnknown.message: Cost: unknown – prices are shown under “Choose model”

ctxAlsoSent.message: Also sent: whether the sender is in your address book and how many of their mails in this folder you opened (the address book itself stays local).

detectNewslettersHint.message: Checks the visible mails for unsubscribe information (List-Unsubscribe header or a note in the text) and shows a “Newsletter” tag. Read from your mail server only – nothing is sent anywhere.

emptyNoMatchHint.message: Nothing matches the search, group or spam filter.

errAuth.message: The API key was rejected (invalid or out of credit).

errBadJson.message: The response was not valid JSON.

errDecisionViaChat.message: “$1” is a decision model – it can't chat, so as a language model it only produces meaningless text. Choose “Decision model” instead, with provider Ollama, “LM Studio (Jev-Style 2B v1)” or “Jev-Style server”.

errEmptyReply.message: The model returned an empty reply (is it a text model?).

errLocalOrigin.message: The local server at $1 refuses requests from Thunderbird (newer jev-style versions do that by default). Start it with the option --allow-any-host.

errNoLetters.message: The model doesn't answer in the decision format (it wanted to say $1). In LM Studio only Jev-Style 2B v1 works.

errNoLogprobs.message: The server returned no token probabilities (logprobs) – update LM Studio or use llama-server.

errNoUsableJson.message: The model did not return usable JSON – please choose another model.

errNotDecision.message: Unexpected response – is this really a decision model?

errNotFound.message: Model “$1” was not found at the provider.

errOllama403Manual.message: Ollama still rejects requests from Thunderbird (403). Allow Thunderbird in Ollama – in a terminal: $1 – then quit and restart Ollama.

errOllaya403.message: Ollaya rejects requests from Thunderbird (403). Quit it and start it with Thunderbird allowed: $1 – or “Allow access” lets the add-on talk to Ollaya like a local app.

errOllaya403Manual.message: Ollaya still rejects requests from Thunderbird (403). Quit the running Ollaya and start it like this in a terminal: $1

errOllayaPull.message: Ollaya doesn't have the model “$1” yet. Download it once in a terminal: $2

errOrigin403.message: $1 rejects requests from Thunderbird (403). “Allow access” lets the add-on talk to $1 like a local app.

errOriginShort.message: $1 blocks Thunderbird (403) – allow the add-on's access when Thunderbird asks, then test again.

errParse.message: The model returns no usable answers – please choose another model.

errServerDown.message: $1 is not reachable. Start it in a terminal: $2

errSlotModelViaLm.message: “$1” (Jev-Style 0.8B v3 / 2B v4) can't be read through LM Studio – its score sits inside the model. Load Jev-Style 2B v1 in LM Studio, or run this model with “jev-style serve” and choose provider “Jev-Style server”.

jevHint.message: Install once: `pip install "jev-style[mlx]"` (Apple silicon) or `pip install "jev-style[torch]"`, then start: `$2`. Runs the current Jev-Style 0.8B v3 (add `--release 2b` for the 2B v4). The add-on expects it at $1 – another port goes under “Advanced” (e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:8766`).

keyWillBeRemoved.message: will be removed when you save

lmDecisionHint.message: In LM Studio, load `Jev-Style-Qwen3.5-2B-Decision` (v1) and start the local server. The add-on asks for one token and reads the probabilities of “yes”/“no” – the same calibrated score. Newer Jev-Style models (0.8B v3, 2B v4) can't be read through LM Studio – use “Jev-Style server” for them.

privacyBody.message: Sent to $1: sender and subject, plus up to $2 characters of the mail text. The excerpt improves detection considerably.

provDecisionDesc.message: A classifier that doesn't write text: one calibrated spam probability per mail. Fast, cheap, reliable – no LLM.

provLlmDesc.message: A language model reads several mails per request and rates them. Flexible, but slower – the cost depends on the model.

pvTrustTitle.message: Always trust this sender address (never spam)

retryTitle.message: Score the mails that failed last time again

settingsSub.message: How should your mails be scored?

shortcutsSub.message: Clean up faster, without the mouse.

srcHintCustom.message: Any server with an OpenAI-compatible chat API (e.g. llama-server, vLLM) – enter its address under “Advanced”.

srcHintCustomDecision.message: Another server with OpenRouter's Decisions API or the Jev-compatible `/v1/systemone` – enter its address under “Advanced”.

srcHintDeepSeek.message: DeepSeek's own models at low prices.

srcHintGroq.message: Open models (Llama, Qwen …) on very fast hardware. Free tier with rate limits.

srcHintLmStudio.message: Install LM Studio, download a model (e.g. Qwen3 4B or Llama 3.2 3B) and start the local server (Developer tab, or `lms server start`). If LM Studio requires an API token, enter it as the key. Nothing leaves your computer.

srcHintOllama.message: Install Ollama, then run `ollama pull llama3.2:3b` in a terminal. No key, no cost, nothing leaves your computer. Thunderbird asks once for access so the add-on can reach Ollama.

srcHintOllaya.message: Ollaya runs open decision models on your computer, the way Ollama runs LLMs. Install once: `curl -fsSL https://ollaya.dev/install.sh | sh` (macOS on Apple silicon, Linux; Windows: see the website), then `ollaya pull laya:en` (≈ 850 MB; handles German mail well too) and start it with Thunderbird allowed: `OLLAYA_ORIGINS='moz-extension://*' ollaya serve` (without it, Ollaya refuses add-ons with 403). No key needed, nothing leaves your computer; Thunderbird asks once for access.

srcHintOpenAI.message: OpenAI's GPT models. Paid – the API account needs credit (separate from a ChatGPT subscription).

srcHintOpenRouter.message: One key for hundreds of models from many providers, some of them free. “Choose model…” shows the price of each.

srcHintOrDecision.message: Decision models via OpenRouter's Decisions API. `respan/span-01-lite:free` is free (about 20 mails per minute), `typesafe/jev-1.14` is faster and paid. The OpenRouter key also works for language models.

srcHintTogether.message: Many open models, billed per token.
